title: Polysemantic neurons
description: Individual neurons respond strongly to apparently unrelated inputs.

coverage.scope_note: This snapshot contains the saved merged final records used by this entry, including records not individually shown on the page. It is not an exhaustive collection of experiments or papers. Missing records, omitted extraction and not-tested statements are different from negative results.

claims.heading: Some neurons in image classifiers respond to several unrelated kinds of input
Many MLP neurons in transformer language models fire on unrelated inputs, varying by layer
Neurons are polysemantic because networks squeeze more sparse features into fewer neurons (superposition)
Polysemantic neurons also arise from initialization, regularization or training noise, not just capacity limits
Activation, architecture and regularization change the polysemantic-neuron share and can lower it cheaply
Do better tools show polysemantic neurons mostly detect one feature or related offshoots?
Whether a neuron looks polysemantic depends on activation range and scoring method

related_findings.title: Learned directions are more monosemantic than single neurons
related_findings.summary: Across language, vision, audio, protein and other models, directions found by SAEs, sparse coding, PCA, k-means or NMF score as more monosemantic or interpretable than single neurons or basis dimensions. In at least one model, VGG16, they score about the same.

examples.headline: Llama 3.1 8b neurons score near random on explanation quality, well below trained SAEs.
In four of five CNNs, learned directions match their concept labels more precisely than single neurons.
In Qwen2-Audio, top SAE features score far more monosemantic than top residual dimensions.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: SAE design choices change how monosemantic latents are
related_findings.summary: Dictionary width and sparsity, encoder architecture, regularizers and concept supervision all shift how monosemantic sparse-dictionary latents are. The gains often come at some cost in reconstruction.

examples.headline: Off-support penalties raise Top-k vision SAE monosemanticity at matched reconstruction; one SigLIP2 setting barely moves.
Matryoshka SAEs show far less first-letter absorption than larger BatchTopK SAEs.
A Parity Bottleneck shows far less absorption than TopK or Matryoshka SAEs, but lower automated-interpretability scores.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Architecture and training change how many units align with concepts
related_findings.summary: Architecture choices (such as mixture-of-experts, weight sparsity and where SoLU is used), width, training data and regularization all change how many units match single concepts, or what indirect measures of superposition show. The direction of the effect differs by model and measure.

examples.headline: Widening AlexNet conv5 to 768 units adds concept detectors; going wider brings no significant gain.
In chess GPT-2-like models, MoEs (MoE-X, Switch) cover more board-state features than GELU; SoLU covers fewer.
A Concept Diversity Regularizer adds interpretable neurons in ResNet-18 but cuts them in ResNet-50.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Neuron labels and interpretability scores depend on the method
related_findings.summary: The concept a neuron is credited with, the share of neurons judged interpretable or selective, and which neurons get picked all shift with the scoring metric, threshold, probing data, activation range and explainer model.

examples.headline: In most face CNNs tested, Hierarchical Network Dissection judges more units interpretable than Network Dissection.
LLM concept-neuron selectivity drops sharply out-of-sample; clamping a top neuron degrades output without inducing the concept.
An Opus 5.5 explainer pipeline outscores GPT-4's on all 20 shared GPT-2 XL neurons.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Applied SAE latents are mostly, not fully, monosemantic
related_findings.summary: SAE latents trained on vision, pathology, recommender, EEG and language models are largely but not fully monosemantic. Labels drawn from top activations can misstate what a latent does causally.

examples.headline: A pathologist judged most pathology-SAE concepts monosemantic: 75% on Camelyon16, 86% on PANDA.
Most vision SAE configurations score near-maximal Connectivity (feature overlap), which the authors read as polysemanticity.
Deactivating CLIP SAE gender latents barely moves gender skew, while age latents lower it.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: SAE latent scores depend on activation range and evaluation setup
related_findings.summary: Whether a sparse-dictionary latent looks monosemantic depends on which activations are inspected, since many look coherent only at the top, and on the scoring metric, embedding space and evaluation harness.

examples.headline: In gelu-2l, attention SAE features are specific at high activations but polysemantic lower down.
Embedding-based monosemanticity scores rise the more alike the scoring encoder's embeddings are: CLIP highest, DINOv3 lowest.
Tightly capping the judge model's replies can collapse protein SAE odd-one-out scores; prompt wording shifts them.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Interpretable features spread across many neurons
related_findings.summary: In trained networks, interpretable features mostly do not line up with single neurons. Each spreads over many neurons, so ablating or protecting neurons does not single out one feature.

examples.headline: In gelu-1l, about 92% of SAE feature decoder vectors are dense in the neuron basis.
In Gemma-2 9B-it, a median MLP neuron's output draws on 500-1350 SAE features.
In AlexNet fc1, 80% of activation variance needs 42 PCs but 2782 neurons.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Toy-model superposition depends on data, architecture and training
related_findings.summary: In toy models, how much superposition forms and what geometry it takes depend on feature sparsity, correlation and importance, bottleneck width, activation function, choice of training loss, dropout, weight decay and decoder depth. The resulting loss differs little between these solutions.

examples.headline: Widening the toy bottleneck from d=5 to d=20 lowers superposition metrics.
Superposition varies strongly across activation functions while loss stays in a narrow range.
Two toy-model features point opposite in 0.068 of training runs if uncorrelated, 0.562 if never co-occurring.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Absorption, hedging and co-occurrence make SAE latents polysemantic
related_findings.summary: Sparse-dictionary latents become polysemantic through feature absorption, hedging and concept co-occurrence. This happens both when the dictionary is too narrow or too sparse and when width suffices but the sparsity objective favours merging.

examples.headline: A Gemma Scope 'starts with S' latent doesn't fire on 'short'; a token-specific latent absorbs it.
Feature hedging falls steeply with SAE width but stays nonzero at width 65536.
In GPT-2 and Pythia-410M SAEs, 18-36% of active features don't distinguish the senses of polysemous words.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Multi-response units often fire for related or look-alike concepts
related_findings.summary: Units that respond to several inputs often respond to related, co-occurring or visually similar concepts, such as facets, sub-concepts, antonyms, related languages or a shared positional property, rather than unrelated ones.

examples.headline: The more neurons two concepts share in Pythia, the more similar humans rate them (correlation 0.70-0.79).
A multi-motif protein SAE latent matches 17 motifs, all at the protein C-terminus.
The CNN filters picked for co-occurring or look-alike concepts overlap by up to 93%.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Some single neurons are selective and causally drive outputs
related_findings.summary: Some individual neurons are selective for one concept, rule or language and causally drive matching outputs, sometimes matching or beating SAE features. These are selected neurons, not estimates of how common such neurons are.

examples.headline: Llama1B and Llama8B raw MLP neurons beat SAE features as 1-D probes across 113 binary tasks.
About 913 of 2,048 layer-5 OthelloGPT neurons match decision-tree rules; ablating them lowers targeted legal-move probability.
Ablating a selected 0.5% neuron set cuts target-emotion accuracy about 11-15 points; others barely move.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Real-model activations look like sparse, overcomplete feature mixtures
related_findings.summary: Activations of trained language, vision and biology models are well described as sparse combinations of more feature directions than dimensions. Small task-specific models may show little of this structure.

examples.headline: Pythia-410M SAEs imply a critical width above the 1,024-wide residual stream at three layers.
All layers of four BERT models appear sparse, most at the embedding layer.
Counterpoint: single-layer PatchTST forecasting models show only weak SAE signatures of superposition.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Attention heads and MoE experts are often polysemantic too
related_findings.summary: Units other than MLP neurons are often polysemantic: one attention head or MoE expert serves several unrelated behaviours or domains. How monosemantic experts are varies with routing sparsity and depth.

examples.headline: Only 14 of 144 GPT-2 Small attention heads looked plausibly monosemantic.
Pythia-1.4B head L12H0 does successorship, acronyms, greater-than and copying.
SAE latents best predicting an MoE expert's routing form 10.8-11.3 distinct clusters on average, not one.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Many units in other models lack a single-concept description
related_findings.summary: Beyond InceptionV1 and language-model MLPs, a sizeable share of neurons in CNNs, ViTs, audio, tabular, vision-language-action and LLM models has no simple single-concept description. Multi-concept explanations predict their activations better.

examples.headline: Under one concept-match cutoff, 69.7% of ResNet-18 and 77.8% of ResNet-50 neurons count as interpretable.
An LLM judge rates 46.9% of sampled Qwen-2.5-32B-Instruct MLP neurons polysemantic, 20.2% monosemantic.
Only 6 of 20 sampled pi0.5-DROID layer-5 FFN neurons were labelled interpretable.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Theory and limits of computing in superposition
related_findings.summary: In principle, networks can store and compute more sparse features than they have neurons, up to capacity limits set by interference. In one study, small trained Boolean MLPs stop at about one feature per neuron.

examples.headline: Theory: sparse-input ReLU MLPs can compute far more Boolean features than they have neurons.
In hand-built ReLU MLPs computing 557 circuits in superposition, errors grow with depth and active-circuit count.
Small trained Boolean MLPs start erring once clause count reaches hidden width.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Units chosen for one task also serve others
related_findings.summary: Neurons or parameters selected for one task, concept or behaviour also contribute to others, so ablating or editing them has off-target effects. One study finds the shared neurons peripheral.

examples.headline: Unrelated knowledge statements in one LLM share up to 18% of activated neurons.
In a multitask model, conditioning on one unit's ablation-mask marginal cuts task entropy by about 4.21%; conditioning on the full mask cuts it by 82.6% on average.
Counterpoint: ablating all 26 neurons shared between SmolLM3-3B behaviour circuits had no effect.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Superposition linked to adversarial and noise vulnerability
related_findings.summary: Superposition raises vulnerability to adversarial attacks and noise and can cause behavioural errors. Adversarial training can reduce it by dropping low-amplitude features, but whether it rises or falls under adversarial training depends on task demand relative to capacity.

examples.headline: Under label noise, SAE and non-negative contrastive features beat contrastive ones by up to 13.7 points.
Adversarial (PGD) perturbations align closely with feature-interference directions; correlated features make attacks transfer across seeds.
An adversarially trained toy model drops exactly the 70 low-amplitude non-robust features.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Residual-stream and embedding dimensions mix several concepts
related_findings.summary: Basis dimensions of the residual stream and of embeddings carry several classes or concepts at once. In some tests they are no more interpretable than random directions.

examples.headline: In BERT sentence embeddings, random directions look patterned as often as basis neurons.
Over 60% of GPT-2's most salient hidden dimensions are shared between both IMDB classes.
In Llama3-8B-Instruct, 17.55% of last-layer coordinates matter for every ethical persona; chance level is not reported.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Neuron alignment depends on a privileged basis
related_findings.summary: How far features align with single neurons depends on a basis privileged by the activation function and training. Rotating the basis, or using multiplicative gating, moves structure out of single units without changing accuracy.

examples.headline: A random rotation of AlexNet conv5 cuts unique detectors by 80% without hurting discrimination.
In modular-addition Transformers, GLU variants concentrate Fourier structure in top PCs, not single neurons.
Softplus RNNs have far more task-specialized units than tanh RNNs, which specialize in subspaces.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Unit content and polysemanticity vary with depth
related_findings.summary: In vision and audio classifiers, what units detect and how polysemantic or hard to describe they are change with depth, but studies disagree on whether polysemanticity peaks in middle or late layers. The original SoLU paper reports, qualitatively, language-model neuron roles shifting from de-tokenizing to abstract concepts to re-tokenizing.

examples.headline: In a vision CNN, polysemanticity is higher in layer4 than in layer3.
CLIP-based neuron descriptions rate best in conv1 and layer4 of ResNets, worse mid-network.
In ResNet152 and CLIP-ResNet50 examples, the CPE polysemanticity score peaks at intermediate stages.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Polysemantic neurons can be split into cleaner sub-units
related_findings.summary: A polysemantic neuron's distinct responses can run through separable upstream inputs, input weights or downstream heads. Splitting along these paths yields more monosemantic sub-units without changing model outputs.

examples.headline: Splitting selected CNN channels by previous-layer inputs yields two class-specific channels.
Rewiring an already trained ViT splits units into more semantically coherent subunits, leaving accuracy unchanged.
CLIP-ResNet neuron contributions span more than one direction; each neuron-attention-head pair's contribution spans one.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Units that recur across seeds or models are more interpretable
related_findings.summary: Few neurons recur across seeds or models, and those that do tend to be more interpretable. Superposed features are arranged differently across seeds, and polysemanticity concentrates in units that do not recur.

examples.headline: 1.23-4.16% of GPT-2 and Pythia neurons recur across seeds; selected recurring ones usually have clear interpretations.
Toy models from different seeds arrange the same features in different superposition patterns.
Neuron interpretability scores predict recurrence across models in all 12 vision-model pairs, more weakly in LLMs.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Superposition and interpretability measures shift during training
related_findings.summary: Superposition and unit-interpretability measures change during training, some settling early and some late. Studies disagree on whether superposition grows or shrinks as training goes on.

examples.headline: Effective feature count consolidates sharply at grokking, tracking the local learning coefficient (a complexity measure).
Highly non-Gaussian neurons emerge within about 10-20B tokens of Pythia training.
ResNet50 neurons are already less interpretable than activation clusters at initialization.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Language-model neuron monosemanticity changes with model scale
related_findings.summary: Most of these studies find the importance and monosemanticity of single language-model neurons falling with model size, while one finds concept specialization rising. Two, one of them anecdotal, report broad neurons splitting into narrower ones in larger models.

examples.headline: Ablating one context-detecting neuron costs 8% in a 70M model but 0.2% in a 6.9B model.
In pre-trained Pythia 70M-6.9B, several indicators show monosemanticity falling with scale.
Against the trend, MLP value vectors (neuron output weights) are more concept-specialized in larger, newer LLMs.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Units mix features even with spare capacity
related_findings.summary: Units can mix several features even when capacity is ample. The reported drivers are the data distribution (for example, whether the latent variables behind the data can be negative and which values they can take), noise statistics, regularization and SGD itself.

examples.headline: In overcomplete toy MLPs, many specialized neurons still spread activation across clusters.
With weight decay and one neuron per latent, signed or log-normal latents lose one-to-one neuron alignment.
In biologically constrained networks, latent variables' ranges and support, not their dependence, govern neuron mixing.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Heavy-tailed statistics single out a minority of distinct neurons
related_findings.summary: Heavy-tailed activation or vocabulary-projection statistics, such as kurtosis, skew or non-Gaussianity, pick out a minority of distinct neurons. Kurtosis studies read these neurons as monosemantic, while studies of non-Gaussian outputs call them entangled.

examples.headline: In Qwen3-32B layer-0 neurons, higher kurtosis goes with more lexically concentrated extreme activations.
A small group of highly non-Gaussian FFN neurons appears in Pythia-1.4B, Llama-2-7B and Llama-3-8B.
Gemma-2-2B's top 100 neurons by a gradient-based score (delta-x-grad) have sharper peaks than neurons overall.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Unit-level analyses fragment multi-dimensional features
related_findings.summary: Some features are multi-dimensional, such as circles or manifolds. Neurons or SAE atoms that each cover part of one can then look like several narrow features.

examples.headline: SAE clusters recover circular representations of days and months in GPT-2 and Mistral 7B.
InceptionV1 curve neurons each cover a narrow orientation range; one subspace (Grassmannian block) spans all orientations.
SAE decoder clusters have more vectors than PCA dimensions needed to explain 80% of their variance.

reading_list.why: The original example: InceptionV1 neuron 4e:55 (cat faces, car fronts, cat legs), with an untested superposition explanation.
Reports an architecture change raising blind-rated interpretable neurons from about 35% to about 60% at similar loss; the gain shrinks in the largest model.
A rare random-sample estimate: 31% of 128 ResNet-18 units fire for unrelated concepts, under a lenient criterion.

known_gaps.summary: How common polysemantic neurons are and whether they mix unrelated concepts remain unsettled, the canonical InceptionV1 neuron has not been independently re-examined, causal accounts and architectural fixes rest mostly on toy and small models, and several central works are not yet covered.
items: How common polysemantic neurons are in language models is unsettled: the two counts use different definitions and disagree, with under 5% of neurons per layer in Pythia-70M and GPT-2 Small (by a sparse-autoencoder criterion) against 46.9% in Qwen-2.5-32B-Instruct (by one LLM judge). Studies also disagree on which layers are most polysemantic, and no model above 100B parameters has a count.

Whether polysemantic neurons mostly mix related or unrelated concepts is open. The main random-sample estimate covers one ResNet-18 layer under a lenient criterion, and the language-model evidence is mostly qualitative, some of it from the original authors' group.

The canonical InceptionV1 neuron 4e:55 has not been independently re-examined. Studies of Inception models each use a different criterion for 'unrelated', so no share of polysemantic units in InceptionV1 can be stated.

Evidence that superposition causes polysemanticity comes mainly from toy models. In real networks it rests on few studies, and comparisons of sparse-autoencoder features with neurons are correlational.

Polysemanticity with at least as many neurons as features has been shown only in toy models, mainly with an L1 activation penalty that is uncommon in practice. Other toy studies find that when neurons exactly match features in number and weight decay is used, mixing depends on the data distribution, so the role of regularization is unresolved.

Evidence that architecture or training changes cut polysemanticity without a large loss comes from toy models and from small or unstated-size networks, and one CNN study reports no accuracy for its sparsity-penalty runs. A language model designed to have interpretable neurons has worse loss than GPT-2, no other group has re-measured SoLU's interpretable-neuron rate, and a chess-model study and toy-model studies give mixed results on SoLU.

Several central works are not yet among the studies drawn on here: Feature Visualization (2017), Multimodal Neurons (2021), Polysemanticity and Capacity in Neural Networks (2022), Towards Monosemanticity (2023) and Bills et al. (2023) on LLM-written neuron explanations. Any of them could change the picture on prevalence and on superposition as a cause.
